authority_basis.summary: Derive or falsify a source-derived noncircular boundary quotient of Mellin dilation with discrete xi spectrum.

operations.title: The primitive Mobius half-line has the wrong Weyl law for zeta zeros
operations.statement: Granting the candidate primitive Mobius carrier a circumference L and holonomy eta=plus or minus one, logarithmic dilation -i d/dy has arithmetic-progression spectrum and positive counting law L*T/(2*pi)+O(1). Zeta-zero ordinates have Riemann-von Mangoldt growth T/(2*pi) log(T/(2*pi))-T/(2*pi)+O(log T). No L or available holonomy can repair the asymptotic mismatch.
operations.scope: Falsifies the direct compact-circle realization of the conditional primitive half-line; does not exclude infinite, energy-dependent, or higher-dimensional source-derived systems.

operations.title: Mobius-circle Weyl-law hostile test
operations.procedure: Impose periodic and antiperiodic holonomy on -i d/dy over a circle of length L, compute its exact spectrum and counting law, and compare leading growth with Riemann-von Mangoldt.
operations.expected_result: Both holonomies give linear spectral growth, incompatible with T log T for every fixed L. Matching asymptotic growth would falsify the no-go.

operations.title: Grothendieck reports the Mobius half-line Weyl-law obstruction
operations.body: I tested the primitive Mobius half-line as the most favorable direct boundary quotient of Mellin dilation. Even granting the missing PC quotient, a metric length L, and holonomy eta=plus/minus one, -i d/dlog x has arithmetic-progression spectrum with linear count L*T/(2*pi)+O(1), whereas zeta zeros have T log T Riemann-von Mangoldt growth. Thus the topology/sign system cannot be the Hilbert-Polya boundary by itself. Any viable replacement needs infinite or energy-dependent phase-space volume; Ledger 1367 records the exact no-go.
